papers.title: Concordance between target trial emulation and randomised controlled trials: systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.one_line: Across 107 emulation and trial pairs from 50 studies, agreement is moderate at Pearson 0.59 and a pooled ratio of ratios of 0.96, rising to Pearson 0.83 in the 63 pairs meeting close emulation criteria, with a multivariable model of nine design features explaining only 9.2% of the variance in concordance.
papers.what_was_done: Systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis of observational studies that explicitly emulated a named randomized trial of a drug, surgical procedure or device, searched across five databases from 2010 to October 2025 and registered as PROSPERO CRD42024619811. Fifty studies yielding 107 emulation and trial pairs were assessed against 21 predefined design features and eight agreement metrics, including standardized difference agreement, estimate agreement, agreement on statistical significance, Pearson and intraclass correlation, percentage deviation, and ratio of ratios. Risk of bias used RoB 2 for the trials and ROBINS-I for the emulations. Subgroup analyses covered outcome type, data source, disease domain, intervention type, confounding adjustment method, estimand, guideline use and registration; sensitivity analyses included leave-one-out cross validation.

future_research.gap: Whether adherence to individual reporting checklist items relates to reporting consistency and reproducibility is unquantified, and the guideline's implementation and possible extensions depend on that evidence.
future_research.quote: Future methodological work should quantify how adherence to checklist items relates to reporting consistency and reproducibility and inform implementation and potential extensions of the guideline.

future_research.gap: The available sample was too small and too unevenly distributed to run multilevel subgroup analyses across combinations of emulation design features, so effect modifiers among design choices remain unexplored.
future_research.quote: Fourthly, owing to the distribution and limited size of the available sample, we were unable to do multilevel subgroup analyses across multiple emulation features.

future_research.gap: Emulation quality was scored from predefined criteria applied to what each study chose to report, so biases outside the checklist and outside the reported text are unmeasured.
future_research.quote: Firstly, our assessment of “emulation quality” relied on predefined criteria and the information reported in each study, so some relevant biases may not have been captured by our checklist.

problems.evidence: Nine of 21 predefined design features were significantly associated with concordance, and hospital initiation and outcome emulation quality survived multivariable selection. That is the closest thing the field has to an attribution procedure for discordance. It is also explicitly incomplete: the fitted model accounts for 9.2% of the variance, so more than nine tenths of the variation in how far an emulation lands from its trial is not attributed to any measured design feature.
problems.quote: closer outcome emulation and treatment not started in hospital were associated with target trial emulation-randomised controlled trial concordance

problems.evidence: Benchmarking against a trial is the field's main validation device, and its own yield is moderate rather than strong: 79% standardized difference agreement but only 50% full agreement on statistical significance, with Pearson 0.59 across the broad sample against 0.82 in the narrower RCT-DUPLICATE claims sample. Whether a benchmarking result transfers to the questions that have no trial is not settled by these numbers.
problems.quote: Most target trial emulation-randomised controlled trial pairs met one or more of the binary agreement metrics for concordance ( table 3 ): standardised difference agreement (85/107; 79%), estimate agreement (82/107; 77%), full agreement for statistical significance (53/107; 50%), and partial agreement for statistical significance (20/41; 49%).
problems.locator: Results, Target trial emulation-randomised controlled trial concordance

problems.evidence: Outcome misclassification is identified as a measured driver of discordance rather than a theoretical concern: low clinical specificity and high missingness in the outcome definition track directly with larger emulation to trial gaps, and the proposed remedies are sensitivity analyses and calibration rather than measurement.
problems.quote: In our analysis, lower quality of outcome emulation—for instance, outcomes measured with low clinical specificity or high levels of missingness (for example, laboratory test results such as glycated haemoglobin, administrative definitions of venous thromboembolism, or less well validated composite endpoints)—was associated with greater discrepancies between target trial emulation and randomised controlled trial results.

problems.evidence: The direction of bias is a property of the data source, not only of the analysis: the 50 claims-based pairs underestimate treatment effects as a group, which means an emulation's answer depends on which database it was run in.
problems.quote: Target trial emulations based on claims data tended to underestimate the treatment effects compared with randomised controlled trials (ratio of ratios 0.90, 95% CI 0.82 to 0.99; I 2 =38%; n=50; P=0.03) ( fig 4 ).

problems.evidence: Trials that start treatment in hospital produce discordant emulations because routine databases do not record inpatient initiation or its timing, so time zero cannot be aligned with the trial's. The proposed fixes are to link more data sources or to avoid the setting, neither of which solves alignment where inpatient timing is unrecorded.
problems.quote: Defining time zero in alignment with the trial is a known challenge in target trial emulation studies.

problems.evidence: Population mismatch between the emulated cohort and the index trial degrades concordance measurably, and the review documents a case where a veterans and Medicare cohort was 98.8% male against 66% in the trial, giving standardized differences above 2.1 in both pairs. Whether an emulation can be restricted or reweighted to a trial's population is a data availability question, not a design choice.
problems.quote: In our analysis, greater differences in age and sex distributions between the emulated cohort and the corresponding randomised controlled trial were associated with lower concordance of effect estimates.

problems.evidence: Bias direction is outcome-specific and does not cancel: venous thromboembolism and major adverse cardiovascular events are systematically underestimated while respiratory outcomes are overestimated, so an aggregate concordance statistic conceals opposing errors by outcome type.
problems.quote: In subgroup analyses, compared with randomised controlled trials, target trial emulations consistently underestimated the outcomes of venous thromboembolism (ratio of ratios 0.76, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.00; I 2 =40%; n=9; P=0.05) or major adverse cardiovascular events (0.91, 0.86 to 0.96; I 2 =32%; n=29; P<0.001), but overestimated respiratory outcomes (1.20, 1.03 to 1.40; I 2 =40%; n=5; P=0.02)

problems.evidence: Two thirds of benchmarking emulations follow no reporting guidance at all, and the eleven that cite one cite STROBE, which has no target trial protocol component. Reporting practice in the subset of studies most exposed to scrutiny does not reach the level the design requires.
problems.quote: Among these studies, 17 (34%) publicly registered their protocol and 16 (32%) followed published reporting guidelines, either STROBE (n=11), International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research (ISPOR; n=3), both STROBE and ISPOR (n=1), or Reporting of Studies Conducted Using Observational Routinely Collected Health Data (n=1).

problems.evidence: Every benchmarking emulation in the sample was run after its index trial was published, and only a third carry a public protocol, so a concordance literature cannot rule out that discordant emulations were not published. The headline agreement figures are conditional on that.
problems.quote: Lastly, selective reporting is an important consideration in benchmarking studies. In this review, only 34% (17/50) of target trial emulation studies reported a publicly accessible protocol or registration; although this may improve transparency, it is not directly analogous to trial registration and cannot rule out selective non-publication, particularly as all included benchmarking emulations were conducted after publication of the index randomised controlled trial.

problems.evidence: Of 541 full texts reviewed, 445 were dropped because the emulation named no trial to emulate. The overwhelming majority of published emulations therefore state a target trial that cannot be checked against anything, which is the condition that makes trial-choice justification unverifiable.
problems.quote: At full text review, most exclusions (445/541; 82%) were for hypothetical trial emulations.

problems.evidence: Adjustment method is not what separates a concordant emulation from a discordant one. Matching and doubly robust estimation both leave moderate heterogeneity, and the estimand category shows no association with concordance at all, which locates the residual gap in design and data rather than in the confounding estimator.
problems.quote: Regarding confounding adjustment methods, both the matching method and the doubly robust method showed good concordance with moderate heterogeneity (supplementary figure G).

papers.title: The importance of the design of observational studies in comparative effectiveness research: Lessons from the GARFIELD-AF and ORBIT-AF registries.
papers.one_line: The same target trial of vitamin K antagonist versus no anticoagulation was emulated in two atrial fibrillation registries and reproduced the randomized mortality and stroke benefit in both, but produced a bleeding hazard ratio of 1.40 in GARFIELD-AF and 1.06 in ORBIT-AF because the two registries define time zero differently.
papers.what_was_done: A target trial of vitamin K antagonist versus no anticoagulation was specified and emulated identically in GARFIELD-AF cohorts 1 and 2 (12,832 naive patients with CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 or more, 7460 treated) and ORBIT-AF I (5944 patients, 4457 treated), with 2-year follow-up, intention-to-treat contrast, and inverse probability of treatment weighting on a shared 27-variable list. Mortality hazard ratios were 0.66 (CI 0.56 to 0.79) in GARFIELD-AF and 0.54 (CI 0.42 to 0.69) in ORBIT-AF; stroke or systemic embolism 0.70 (CI 0.54 to 0.92) and 0.42 (CI 0.22 to 0.80). Major bleeding was 1.40 (CI 1.02 to 1.91) in GARFIELD-AF and 1.06 (CI 0.70 to 1.61) in ORBIT-AF. Reference randomized meta-analyses gave odds ratios of 0.74 for mortality and 0.36 for stroke against placebo. GARFIELD-AF enrolls within 6 weeks of diagnosis so time zero is treatment start; ORBIT-AF enrolls prevalent users whose treatment began months or years earlier. Positivity was checked by tabulating empty covariate cells and by truncating weights at the 1st, 5th and 10th percentiles: mean weights were 1.99 with a maximum of 39.18 in GARFIELD-AF and 2.03 with a maximum of 57.21 in ORBIT-AF, and truncation moved the ORBIT-AF bleeding hazard ratio from 1.06 to 1.24. In the comparator arm, over 70% of patients in both registries received antiplatelet therapy.

future_research.gap: Confounders specific to the treatment decision are not captured by either registry and would have to be designed in prospectively
future_research.quote:
For this reason, it is important to make all possible efforts
during the design stage of an observational study to identify and capture such information.

problems.evidence: Two registries executed the same protocol, the same estimand and the same 27-variable weighting model, and returned bleeding hazard ratios of 1.40 and 1.06 because one enrolls incident and the other prevalent users. The registries were not two estimates of one trial; they emulated different trials, and only the outcome-specific discrepancy revealed it. Pooling them would have produced an intermediate bleeding estimate with no interpretation.
problems.quote:
The main discrepancy between these two registries’
results regarding the known increased risk of bleeding
with VKA suggests that the hypothetical target trial might
not be as well emulated within ORBIT-AF.

problems.evidence: The shared covariate list is structurally aligned and semantically not. The variable entered as prior bleeding is any prior bleed in GARFIELD-AF and gastrointestinal bleeding only in ORBIT-AF; the liver variable is cirrhosis in one and liver disease in the other; the dementia variable is dementia in one and cognitive impairment or dementia in the other. The same weighting model therefore adjusts for different quantities in the two emulations of one trial.
problems.quote: Prior bleeding for GARFIELD-AF, prior gastrointestinal bleeding for ORBIT-AF

problems.evidence: The comparator arm is not untreated. Over 70% of the no-anticoagulant group in both registries received antiplatelet therapy while only 26% and 38% of the treated group did, so the emulated contrast is anticoagulant against antiplatelet, not against nothing. The observational stroke hazard ratios of 0.70 and 0.42 sit against a placebo-controlled randomized odds ratio of 0.36, and the attenuation is attributed to exactly this comparator treatment.
problems.quote:
In GARFIELD-AF and ORBIT-AF, VKA was used in combination with AP therapy in 26% and 38% patients, respectively, whereas over 70% No VKA patients in both
registries received AP.

problems.evidence: A tabular scan for empty cells arising from unusual covariate combinations is a real positivity diagnostic that names covariate strata rather than summarizing weights, and it is executed in both registries. What is reported downstream is still weight behavior: mean 1.99 with maximum 39.18 in GARFIELD-AF, mean 2.03 with maximum 57.21 in ORBIT-AF, and hazard ratios at four truncation levels. No unsupported patient history is named, and no rule says at what weight or what empty-cell count the comparison should not be made.
problems.quote:
In GARFIELD-AF and ORBIT-AF we used a tabular approach to identify empty cells resulting from unusual
combination of factors with small sample sizes.

problems.evidence: One arm is a drug class and the other is an absence defined to permit antiplatelet therapy, so two clinically distinct strategies are pooled into the comparator. The treated arm is equally heterogeneous: the paper flags that vitamin K antagonist therapy depends on international normalized ratio management, with 28% of values below 2 and 17% above 3 in GARFIELD-AF, and 39% of ORBIT-AF treated patients followed in dedicated anticoagulation clinics against 6.6% in the comparison registry.
problems.quote:
Patients
were divided into two groups at the time of study enrolment: those receiving VKA and those not receiving anticoagulant (AC) treatment with or without antiplatelet (AP) agents, defined as No vitamin K antagonist (No VKA) group.

problems.evidence: Time zero in ORBIT-AF is registry enrollment, which for prevalent users falls an unknown interval after treatment start, so early bleeding events accrued during dose titration are missed. That choice was not evaluated by any outcome-blind check; its inadequacy became visible only after the bleeding estimate failed to reproduce the known randomized effect, which makes the time-origin decision adjudicated by the answer it produced.
problems.quote:
Bleeding was more common
than SSE in ORBIT-AF and early bleeding events that accrue while titrating VKA will be missed, due to the misalignment between start of follow-up and start of treatment.

problems.evidence: The only sensitivity analysis reported is weight truncation, varied at four percentile levels. The discussion then names at least three assumptions violated together in ORBIT-AF: prevalent-user selection, confounders such as prior bleeding measured after treatment start, and unmeasured site-level anticoagulation management. None of these is varied, alone or jointly, and the truncation exercise cannot speak to any of them.
problems.quote:
The sensitivity of effect estimates to truncating extreme IPTWs was evaluated to explore the trade-off between reducing confounding bias
and increasing bias and variance because of nonpositivity.

papers.title: Validation of Machine Learning-Based Individualized Treatment for Depressive Disorder Using Target Trial Emulation.
papers.one_line: Super Learner models trained on 715,246 incident depression episodes in Taiwan's claims database achieved areas under the curve of 0.627 and 0.751 and, when the lowest-predicted-failure drug was evaluated by emulated trials, gave treatment failure hazard ratios of 0.84 and 0.82, while conceding the analysis demonstrated associations rather than causal effects.
papers.what_was_done: From 1,853,382 patients coded with depressive disorders in the National Health Insurance Research Database between 2001 and 2013, 745,356 remained after age and diagnosis exclusions, giving 715,246 initial treatment episodes and 739,980 next-step episodes. Treatment failure was a composite claims phenotype: psychiatric hospitalization, self-harm hospitalization, psychiatric emergency visit, or regimen change. Sixteen drug-specific Super Learner models were fitted for initial treatment and 41 for next-step treatment, from 125 and 153 candidate variables reduced by Pearson correlation filtering, with 19 base algorithms combined by the Lawson-Hanson algorithm. Combined areas under the curve were 0.627 (CI 0.623 to 0.630) and 0.751 (CI 0.747 to 0.756). The regimen with the lowest predicted failure probability defined the model-selected strategy. A four-arm target trial was emulated by replicating the study sample four times and enrolling each patient into whichever arm matched their observed treatment: model-selected, treatment as usual, randomly selected by observed prescribing proportions, and randomly selected by recommended proportions. Intention-to-treat hazard ratios for the model-selected arm were 0.84 (CI 0.82 to 0.86), 0.86 (CI 0.82 to 0.89) and 0.92 (CI 0.89 to 0.96) for initial treatment and 0.82 (CI 0.80 to 0.83), 0.85 (CI 0.83 to 0.88) and 0.87 (CI 0.84 to 0.90) for next-step treatment. Baseline failure rates were 26.6% initially and 54.3% at next step.

future_research.gap: Whether the learned treatment rule produces the estimated benefit is untested outside the data that produced it
future_research.quote: Thus, prospective clinical trials are warranted to validate the effectiveness of prediction models for individualized treatment.

problems.evidence: A 19-algorithm ensemble over 153 claims variables is used to build a treatment rule, and the rule is then scored by an emulated trial reporting hazard ratios of 0.84 and 0.82 with intervals two hundredths wide. The same paper concedes that unmeasured factors confound the estimate and that only associations were demonstrated. The flexibility bought a better predictor, not identification, and the causal language survives the concession intact.
problems.quote: Our study only demonstrated associations, rather than causal effects.

problems.evidence: Model choice is settled entirely by predictive discrimination: the Super Learner ensemble is preferred because it beat logistic regression, random forest and support vector machines on the outcome-prediction metric. Nothing evaluates the models on the quantity they are actually used for, which is the ranking of counterfactual failure probabilities across 16 or 41 untaken regimens per patient, and an area under the curve of 0.627 for initial treatment is reported without any bearing on that ranking's reliability.
problems.quote: The performance of the prediction models using the Super Learner ensemble was better than those using logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machine

problems.evidence: The unit of analysis is a treatment episode, and 283,927 patients generate 739,980 next-step episodes, so the same person enters many times and poor responders enter most often. The over-representation is acknowledged as a limitation of interpretation, but the hazard ratio intervals of 0.80 to 0.83 are reported as if episodes were independent, and calendar time across 2001 to 2013 spans changing antidepressant availability with no adjustment.
problems.quote: Second, treatment episodes were used as the basic units of analysis. Therefore, poor responders with multiple treatment episodes were over-represented in the analysis for the next-step treatment.

problems.evidence: The four trial arms are built by replicating the whole sample four times and keeping each patient in the arm their observed treatment matches, which is cloning with censoring in all but name. The reported confidence intervals are as narrow as 0.82 to 0.86 with no statement of how the replication, the arm-specific censoring and the repeated episodes per patient were carried into the variance.
problems.quote: Four study samples were replicated to emulate the clinical trial.
problems.locator: 2.7. Evaluating the Effectiveness of the Machine-Selected Agents in the Test Set

problems.evidence: The learned rule prescribes a distribution of regimens that differs from what clinicians actually prescribe, which means the recommended drug for many patients is one that patients like them rarely received. That is a positivity problem stated as a descriptive observation, with no diagnostic identifying which patient histories have no support for their recommended regimen, and next-step strategies span 41 options including nine augmentations.
problems.quote: The distributions of the model-selected regimens were different from the observed prescription patterns.

problems.evidence: The outcome is a four-part claims phenotype standing in for treatment response, and it is conceded to be insensitive and to detect only the worst outcomes. Symptom severity, function and quality of life are never measured. The binary failure indicator then drives both the trained models and the reported hazard ratios, with no error model relating the phenotype to the clinical state it proxies.
problems.quote: However, these indicators may be insensitive and can only identify the worst conditions.

papers.title: An informatics consult approach for generating clinical evidence for treatment decisions.
papers.one_line: A proof-of-concept Informatics Consult triangulated randomized, meta-analytic, emulated-trial and Mendelian randomization evidence for warfarin in atrial fibrillation with cirrhosis, and the emulation reduced 3,854,710 screened adults to 1022 eligible and 761 matched patients yielding an intention-to-treat mortality hazard ratio of 0.61.
papers.what_was_done: Four evidence streams were generated for a single clinical question: warfarin for stroke prevention in patients who have both atrial fibrillation and liver cirrhosis. A registry search returned no completed randomized trials and four recruiting trials, all of which exclude cirrhosis. A meta-analysis of four observational studies gave a pooled stroke hazard ratio of 0.71 (CI 0.39 to 1.29) with I2 of 73%, and leave-one-out estimates ranging from 0.54 to 0.92. A target trial emulation in CPRD linked to Hospital Episode Statistics and Office for National Statistics death registration screened 3,854,710 adults aged 30 and over, found 1022 eligible individuals (443 initiators, 579 non-initiators), and after propensity score matching on 22 baseline covariates retained 235 initiators and 526 non-initiators. The emulated intention-to-treat hazard ratio was 0.61 (CI 0.49 to 0.76) for all-cause mortality and 0.27 (CI 0.08 to 0.91) for ischaemic stroke, with five prespecified subgroups analyzed by repeating the matching. Phenotypes were code-based, Read version 2 in primary care and ICD-10 in secondary care. Bleeding outcomes and direct oral anticoagulants were not assessed, and prescription data completeness was not quantified.

future_research.gap: Rapid evidence generation at the bedside has no replication, peer review or quality assurance machinery attached to it
future_research.quote: In the context of a more rapid generation of evidence, the Informatics Consult raises new questions about replication, open peer review and quality assurance pipelines.
future_research.locator: Discussion, Developing the informatics consult as a service

future_research.gap: Design and analysis methods for on-demand emulation are not standardized
future_research.quote: Design and analysis methods need to be improved, standardized and widely distributed.
future_research.locator: Discussion, Developing the informatics consult as a service

problems.evidence: A screening population of 3,854,710 adults collapses to 1022 individuals who meet the joint eligibility criteria, and propensity matching removes a further 261, leaving 761 patients to carry a stroke hazard ratio of 0.27 with an interval from 0.08 to 0.91. The database size that justifies the design contributes nothing to the precision of the answer, and no effective sample size is reported alongside the matched counts.
problems.quote: a cohort encompassing 1022 individuals fulfilling all eligibility criteria was created (initiators = 443; non-initiators = 579)
problems.locator: Results, Target trial emulation using population-based EHRs

problems.evidence: Eligibility, exposure and outcome all rest on code-based phenotypes applied as exact binary indicators, with primary care coded in Read version 2 and secondary care in ICD-10. Misclassification is conceded only in narrative form for prescriptions, where unrecorded dispensing would place treated patients in the comparator arm, and none of it is propagated into the reported interval of 0.49 to 0.76.
problems.quote: It is also possible that some prescription data is missing, which means that patients are incorrectly assigned to the control arms.

problems.evidence: Agreement across the streams is asserted as a label rather than measured. The meta-analytic stroke hazard ratio of 0.71 spans 0.39 to 1.29 while the emulated hazard ratio is 0.27 spanning 0.08 to 0.91, and no calibration statistic, standardized difference or estimand alignment check is computed before the two are called concordant and passed to a clinician.
problems.quote: We found broad concordance across the three new sources of evidence we generated.

problems.evidence: Triangulation of an emulation with a meta-analysis of prior observational studies and with Mendelian randomization is an operational attempt to bring an alternative bias structure into the workflow, and it is executed for one question. It stops short of a negative control outcome, a proxy-based correction or validation data, and the residual confounding in the emulated hazard ratio of 0.61 is left unbounded.
problems.quote: it remains difficult to assess whether there unmeasured confounding despite employing causal inference methods

problems.evidence: The deliverable is an electronic health record report summarizing direction of effect for a treating clinician. Diagnosable failures such as covariate imbalance after matching and undiagnosable ones such as unmeasured confounding and missing prescriptions reach the same summary line, and nothing in the returned report separates them.
problems.quote: We provide an overall summary report based on new evidence on warfarin use (lower all-cause mortality and lower stroke risk) in patients with atrial fibrillation and cirrhosis

papers.title: Comparing Effect Estimates in Randomized Trials and Observational Studies From the Same Population: An Application to Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
papers.one_line: An emulation of the VALIDATE trial inside the same SWEDEHEART registry that ran the trial reproduced the null 180-day death and myocardial infarction results but could not reproduce the bleeding outcome or the eligibility criteria, and produced a 1.0% excess death risk at 14 days that the trial never showed.
papers.what_was_done: A target trial with the VALIDATE protocol was emulated in SWEDEHEART for January 2012 to May 2014, the period immediately preceding the trial, comparing bivalirudin with heparin during percutaneous coronary intervention. Six eligibility criteria departed from the trial, including a proxy for terminal disease, unavailable contraindication data, and exclusion of all 3070 patients given any prior heparin because dosage was not recorded. The emulation enrolled 4940 patients (2634 bivalirudin, 2306 heparin) against 6006 randomized in the trial. Inverse probability weighting and outcome regression with standardization were used in pooled logistic models with bootstrap intervals from 500 samples. By 180 days the emulated risk ratio for death was 1.21 (CI 0.88 to 1.68) against a trial hazard ratio of 1.05 (CI 0.78 to 1.41), and for myocardial infarction 1.08 (CI 0.76 to 1.54) against 0.84 (CI 0.60 to 1.19). The bleeding outcome could not be defined as in the trial because registers capture only severe events, and the emulated bleeding risk ratio was 0.69 (CI 0.50 to 0.95) against a trial hazard ratio of 1.00. A 14-day risk difference for death of 1.0% (CI 0.1% to 1.8%) appeared in the emulation only.

future_research.gap: Registries do not record why a treatment was chosen, which is what would identify the confounders driving the early mortality discrepancy
future_research.quote: One way to aid future researchers in identifying significant potential confounders would be if registers included more detailed information on reasons for making treatment decisions.

problems.evidence: The trial ascertained bleeding by phone calls at 7 and 180 days plus hospital record review; the registers capture only the most severe events. The emulation did not produce a noisy version of the trial's bleeding endpoint, it produced a different endpoint, and that different endpoint returned a risk ratio of 0.69 (CI 0.50 to 0.95) where the trial hazard ratio was 1.00. An expanded sensitivity definition still failed to recover the milder events.
problems.quote: Exclusively using the registers, as was done in the target trial, only allowed us to identify the most severe cases of bleeding.

problems.evidence: The trial excluded patients given more than 5000 units of heparin before the procedure. Dose is not in the registry, so an unrecorded criterion was resolved by excluding all 3070 patients with any prior heparin. A sensitivity analysis that excluded none enrolled 7652 instead of 4940 and moved the early death risk difference, showing that the unrecorded criterion silently redefined the population rather than adding noise.
problems.quote: Individuals given >5000 U heparin before PCI in the VALIDATE trial were excluded, but the SWEDEHEART data do not include details on the dosage of heparin administered.

problems.evidence: Sensitivity analyses were run separately over eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, outcomes, confounders, follow-up and analysis. The discussion then attributes the 14-day death discrepancy to two assumptions failing at once, residual confounding by illness severity and an eligibility criterion that could not be emulated, and no analysis varies both together.
problems.quote: Finally, we performed several sensitivity analyses using inverse probability–weighted models to assess the sensitivity of the eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, outcomes, confounders, follow-up, and analysis.

problems.evidence: A 1.0% excess 14-day death risk in the emulation is reported with two candidate explanations, unmeasured severity confounding and imperfect eligibility emulation, and nothing distinguishes them. One of those is checkable against the data and the other is not, yet both leave the same footprint in the published estimate, so a reader cannot tell which assumption to doubt.
problems.quote: could not accurately estimate the comparative risk of death by 14 days, which may be the result of intractable confounding early in follow‐up or the inability to precisely emulate the trial’s eligibility criteria

problems.evidence: Concordance is reported as broad agreement on two of four outcomes, and the comparison sets an emulated risk ratio of 1.21 beside a trial hazard ratio of 1.05 without reconciling the two estimands. The two outcomes that disagreed, bleeding and 14-day death, are discussed narratively rather than folded into a calibration statistic, so the study yields a verdict rather than a measured discrepancy.
problems.quote: There was broad agreement in the estimates for death and MI by 180 days from the trial and the observational emulation of the target trial; both found little differences in risk between patients given heparin and bivalirudin.

problems.evidence: The analysis code is published, which is the part of the transparency gap most often missing. Outcome and covariate definitions live in supplementary tables rather than as executable phenotype logic, weight behavior is summarized only as truncation at the 99th percentile, and the six eligibility departures are described in prose with no record of the alternatives that were rejected.
problems.quote: All analysis codes are available at
problems.locator: Methods, Data, Materials, and Code Disclosure

papers.title: Target trial emulations: bridging the gap between clinical trial and real-world data.
papers.one_line: An editorial commentary endorsing a SCREAM emulation of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist discontinuation after hyperkalaemia, which defined discontinuation by a 6-month grace period among 7408 of 39 518 new users, and concludes that emulations are methodologically superior to naive observational studies.
papers.what_was_done: The commentary frames target trial emulation for a cardiology readership using an accompanying emulation in the Stockholm CREAtinine Measurements healthcare utilization cohort. Among 39 518 new mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist users, 7408 experienced an index hyperkalaemia event; discontinuation was defined as no new dispensation during a 6-month grace period and continuation as at least 6 months of continued use. The rationale for emulation is that a randomized trial is infeasible because fewer than 20% of users experience hyperkalaemia and consent would be difficult in the highest-risk patients. The commentary attributes prevalent user bias and immortal time bias to self-inflicted design choices that emulation removes, and notes that new-user restriction with a 12-month washout eliminated the first. It lists limitations of the emulated study: no data on dose, so the continuation arm may in fact be a dose-reduced arm; no data on doses of concomitant heart failure drugs; and no data on reasons for stopping other than hyperkalaemia. The conclusion is that the findings are reliable and relevant to clinical practice.

future_research.gap: Dose regimens for continuation after hyperkalaemia remain unstudied because dosing data were absent
future_research.quote:
future studies are required to identify appropriate dosages of MRA
and other heart failure medications to continue with

problems.evidence: The verdict on evidence quality is drawn from the design label. Having named the analysis a target trial emulation, the commentary declares the findings reliable and relevant to practice in the same paragraph in which it concedes that residual confounding is always a possibility and that the missing dose data leave the continuation arm undefined. The label carries the credibility that the assumption audit does not support.
problems.quote:
Target trial emulations are methodologically superior to naïve
observational studies, and often yield findings similar to RCTs.

problems.evidence: Both arms are defined by the same 6-month window: discontinuation is no dispensation within it, continuation is use throughout it. No outcome-blind rule produced the six months rather than three or twelve, and the grace period simultaneously sets the assignment rule, the exposure window and the point at which follow-up for the clinical outcomes becomes interpretable.
problems.quote:
MRA discontinuation was defined as no new
dispensation of MRA in a 6-month grace period following the index
hyperkalaemia event, while MRA continuation was defined as at
least 6 months of MRA use following the hyperkalaemia event.

problems.evidence: The continuation arm is a dispensation pattern, not a treatment version. The commentary states that dose was unrecorded and that dose reduction after hyperkalaemia is very likely, which means continuation at full dose and continuation at half dose are pooled into one arm on the strength of the pharmacy record alone, with no criterion for when two dosing patterns count as the same strategy.
problems.quote:
data on MRA dosage
were not available

problems.evidence: Agreement between re-analyzed observational data and randomized results, demonstrated on a set of selected examples, is presented as a general property of the technique and then used to license a heart failure question for which no trial exists and none is expected. No condition is offered under which the demonstrated agreement should be expected to extend to the new question.
problems.quote:
In cases where naïve observational studies
disagree with RCTs, it has been shown that re-analysis of the same
observational data using a target trial emulation technique yields
findings similar to RCTs.

problems.evidence: Residual confounding is named as permanent and then left there. The commentary makes the quality of the emulation entirely a function of the richness of the registry, with no negative control outcome, proxy variable or validation subsample proposed to bound what the registry does not hold, even though it lists three specific unmeasured quantities: dose, concomitant drug dose and reason for stopping.
problems.quote:
Even
then, residual confounding is always a possibility.

papers.title: A trial emulation approach for policy evaluations with group-level longitudinal data.
papers.one_line: Policy trial emulation constructs a separate target trial for each cohort of states adopting a policy on the same date and aggregates across them, illustrated on 42 states in 17 stay-at-home cohorts against 8 never-treated comparison states, where the pre-period placebo estimates for log cases depart from zero badly enough to invalidate the analysis.
papers.what_was_done: The proposal transplants target trial emulation into panel policy evaluation: define exposure, causal contrast, time zero, outcomes, comparison units and estimator separately for each treatment cohort, then aggregate. The worked example uses New York Times tracker dates and daily case counts for United States stay-at-home orders. A single target trial takes the five states adopting on 23 March 2020 against the 8 never-treated states, with 22 March as reference; event-study difference-in-differences estimates with leave-one-unit-out jackknife standard errors serve as both estimate and parallel-trends diagnostic. The nested version repeats this for all 42 adopting states in 17 cohorts, reusing the same 8 comparison states in every trial, and aggregates by days since treatment weighted by cohort size. A naive before-after comparison implied a 0.22 fall in log growth rate. The diagnostics undermine the estimates: pre-period placebo effects for log case growth are near zero only in the ten days before adoption and trend downward before that, and for log cases the placebo estimates depart from zero starkly enough that the analysis is called inappropriate. Both calendar time and case time, indexed to ten days after the tenth confirmed case, are presented as time zero choices.

future_research.gap: Spillover between jurisdictions is unhandled and biases every method presented
future_research.quote: Finally, methods that do not account for spillovers and contagion are likely to be biased in this setting, and so properly addressing interference is a key methodological and practical concern.

future_research.gap: Policies are turned off as well as on and the framework does not model reversal
future_research.quote: Just as in the individual exposure case, modeling individuals or locations turning exposures on AND off is complex.

problems.evidence: A concrete protocol is supplied for a policy intervention: cohort-specific target trials, an explicit time zero for comparison units that never adopt, event-study placebo checks, and cohort-weighted aggregation over 17 cohorts. What it does not supply is a definition of the treatment. Stay-at-home orders differ by state, one tracker's definition is adopted, and heterogeneous requirements are deliberately packaged into a single exposure with the consistency assumption acknowledged as possibly violated.
problems.quote: Instead we consider “packaging treatments” together, allowing for some variation in the specific implementation of the policy across units.

problems.evidence: For an infectious disease policy the no-interference assumption is not a technicality; travel across state lines transmits infection, so a state's case count depends on its neighbors' orders. Nearly all standard tools are said to assume it away, the paper's own difference-in-differences estimates included, and the only remedy pointed to is another study's use of travel and social network data.
problems.quote: nearly all standard tools for policy evaluation assume no interference between units, that is, a state’s outcome only depends on that state’s intervention

problems.evidence: Two time origins are offered, calendar date and days since the tenth confirmed case, and their ordering of states inverts: California is the first adopter in calendar time and a late adopter in case time. The rule for choosing is that it depends on the context, and results under the two are presented in the main text and appendix respectively, so nothing outcome-blind decides which one the estimate comes from.
problems.quote: The choice of time zero will depend on the context.

problems.evidence: Seventeen nested target trials share the same 8 never-treated comparison states, so every control unit participates in every trial and the trials are indexed by adoption date during a 19-day window in which the epidemic itself is moving. The aggregation weights cohorts by treated-unit count and quantifies uncertainty with a leave-one-unit-out jackknife, with no accounting for the repeated participation the reuse creates.
problems.quote: For each cohort, we then emulate a single target trial, selecting the same eight never-treated states as comparisons for every target trial.

problems.evidence: The default panel estimator sidesteps positivity rather than diagnosing it: the parametric outcome model extrapolates from the 8 never-treated states to the 42 adopters without any requirement that adopting and non-adopting states share support. The paper says so directly, and notes that only the doubly robust variants incorporating treatment weighting reintroduce the assumption.
problems.quote: Standard difference-in-difference models avoid positivity by instead relying on a parametric outcome model that potentially extrapolates across groups.

problems.evidence: The estimator space is left open at two levels: the within-trial estimator may be difference-in-differences, inverse propensity weighting, doubly robust estimation, synthetic control, matching or a comparative interrupted time series, and the across-cohort aggregation admits many schemes of which one is chosen. No argument establishes a defensible default and nothing requires a study to show that the choice moved the answer.
problems.quote: There are many ways to aggregate these estimates across cohorts.
problems.locator: Nested target trials, Treatment effect estimation

papers.title: The Need for a Practical Approach to Evaluate the Effectiveness of COVID-19 Vaccines for Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
papers.one_line: A perspective proposing target trial emulation as the practical route to COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness monitoring in low- and middle-income countries, noting that the only prior vaccine emulation was the Israeli BNT162b2 study and that the ChAdOx1 efficacy of 70.4% (95% CI 54.8 to 80.6) did not transfer to South Africa.
papers.what_was_done: The argument is that randomized trials cannot be mounted during mass vaccination campaigns in Africa, where 16% of the world population lives and where the only COVID-19 vaccine trials were conducted in South Africa. The evidentiary anchor is that a vaccine with 70.4% efficacy (95% CI 54.8 to 80.6) against polymerase chain reaction confirmed symptomatic disease more than 14 days after the full dose in a United Kingdom and Brazil population of 11,636 participants showed no protective effect in South Africa where B.1.351 predominated. Target trial emulation is proposed as the framework: specify eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, estimand and analysis plan, then analyze observational data accordingly. Specific design proposals include restricting eligibility to symptomatic presenters through a test-negative design to limit confounding by health-care-seeking behavior, drawing a causal diagram to separate confounders from colliders, handling partial vaccination as time-varying exposure, and using multiple eligibility instances per person for precision. The only prior application named is the Israeli BNT162b2 campaign. Data infrastructure is described qualitatively: OpenMRS is common, digital record coverage varies between countries, and one African CDC cross-sectional effort captured more than 2.5 million cases and more than 65,000 deaths. No emulation is performed.

future_research.gap: The immunological effect of endemic co-infections on vaccine response, which would drive effect modification in the target population, is unknown
future_research.quote: However, the effects of these infections and diseases on the immune response to COVID-19 vaccines are not well understood.

problems.evidence: The transport problem is stated in its sharpest form and then left unaddressed. One randomized estimate of 70.4% failed to hold in a neighboring population because of a variant, and the single existing vaccine emulation comes from Israel with well-organized digital records. Whether the Israeli emulation carries to settings differing in coverage, pace, vaccine type, baseline incidence and circulating variants is called an ongoing debate, and no sampling model or transport estimator is proposed to settle it.
problems.quote: Although the lessons from Israel are highly impactful, their applicability elsewhere is an ongoing source of debate.

problems.evidence: The recommended eligibility restriction is a healthcare-use event: only people who present to primary care with symptoms enter the study. That criterion is proposed to reduce confounding by health-care-seeking behavior while conditioning on a variable that both vaccination and infection influence, and the remedy offered is appropriate sensitivity analyses, which are named rather than specified.
problems.quote: For example, a test-negative design could be used, in which only individuals presenting COVID-19 symptoms to primary care are eligible, to reduce confounding by health-care-seeking behavior and treatment misclassification, with the appropriate sensitivity analyses to address selection bias and lack of generalizability.

problems.evidence: Data adequacy is the load-bearing condition of the whole proposal and it is stated without a threshold. High-quality data are called a requirement, the Israeli success is attributed to well-organized digital records, and coverage in African countries is described as variable with no criterion for the coverage, completeness or linkage level at which an emulation should not proceed.
problems.quote: It is also important to point to the requirements for high-quality data in target trial emulation.

problems.evidence: Multiple eligibility instances per person are recommended purely as a precision device. Nothing in the proposal addresses that the same person then contributes to several emulated trials with correlated outcomes, or that in a rolling campaign the sequential trials are indexed by calendar time during which incidence, circulating variant and vaccine type all change, which is the confounding that the efficiency gain conceals.
problems.quote: Some of these techniques for trial emulation can improve precision of estimates by considering multiple instances of eligibility per individual.

problems.evidence: The exposure is vaccination, but the paper lists schedule differences, handling logistics and health system differences across Africa as things that will change real-world effectiveness. These are treatment versions, and no procedure is offered for deciding which of them may be pooled into one arm of an emulated trial and which define separate strategies.
problems.quote: In addition to these factors, differing vaccination schedules and vaccine-handling logistics, and health systems across Africa could influence the real-world effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines.

problems.evidence: The framework is credited with fixing the problems it merely names. Confounding, selection bias and collider bias are listed, and the claim is that emulation accounts for these considerations and provides comprehensive methodological evaluation, which converts a design vocabulary into a statement about how much residual bias a study carries.
problems.quote: Although risk of bias is always an issue for any non-randomized study, the target trial emulation framework provides comprehensive methodological evaluation of observational data.

papers.title: Randomized Trial Replication Using Observational Data for Comparative Effectiveness of Secukinumab and Ustekinumab in Psoriasis: A Study From the British Association of Dermatologists Biologics and Immunomodulators Register.
papers.one_line: An emulation of the CLEAR trial in the BADBIR psoriasis registry with 1231 patients reached regulatory agreement under nine of ten analytic combinations but estimate agreement flipped depending on whether propensity scores were matched or weighted, with matched risk ratios of 1.44 to 1.55 versus a weighted 1.28.
papers.what_was_done: A pragmatic trial comparing secukinumab with ustekinumab was emulated in BADBIR against the CLEAR head-to-head randomized trial, using 1231 patients (314 secukinumab, 917 ustekinumab) initiating between September 2013 and September 2018. The outcome was achieving a Psoriasis Area and Severity Index of 2 or lower at 12 months, recorded for only 42.0% of the secukinumab cohort and 45.5% of the ustekinumab cohort. Two propensity score approaches, 1:1 nearest neighbor matching with caliper 0.05 giving 622 patients and inverse probability weighting, were crossed with five missing outcome methods: complete case, nonresponder imputation, inverse probability of censoring weighting, last observation carried forward and multiple imputation. Agreement with CLEAR was scored on three metrics from Franklin: regulatory agreement, estimate agreement and standardized difference. Under weighting, complete case gave a risk ratio of 1.28 (CI 1.06 to 1.55) and a risk difference of 11.9% (1.6 to 22.1). Under matching, complete case gave 1.55 (1.19 to 2.01), nonresponder imputation 1.45 (1.04 to 2.03), censoring weighting 1.50 (1.14 to 1.96) and multiple imputation 1.44 (1.07 to 1.94), all breaking estimate agreement. Efficacy exceeded real-world effectiveness by 17.5% for secukinumab and 15.1% for ustekinumab.

future_research.gap: Whether the replication survives when the reference trial result is unknown to the analysts has not been tested
future_research.quote: To further test the robustness of this process, the method should be repeated using BADBIR data to conduct a comparative effectiveness study of drugs with corresponding, ongoing RCTs.

future_research.gap: The registry cannot support the reference trial's own primary endpoint
future_research.quote: Because BADBIR does not require recording of data at 16 weeks, we were unable to use the primary end point of PASI 90 at week 16 in the CLEAR trial as the benchmark effect estimate.

problems.evidence: Ten analytic combinations were run on one dataset and the replication verdict depends on which one is read. Propensity weighting reached estimate agreement under every missing-data method except nonresponder imputation for the risk difference, while matching broke estimate agreement for the risk ratio under four of five. Neither estimator is argued to be the default, and the disagreement is reported as a discrepancy rather than resolved.
problems.quote: However, a discrepancy was found regarding which method achieved estimate agreement.

problems.evidence: Three agreement metrics are computed, and the standardized difference is a genuinely calibrated comparison: last observation carried forward with matching gave 0.009 for the risk ratio and minus 0.003 for the risk difference. What remains binary is the verdict that gets carried forward, because regulatory and estimate agreement are pass or fail labels that flip between matched and weighted analyses of the same 1231 patients, and no rule says which label the field should record.
problems.quote: All methods to account for missing outcome data, except NRI in the PS weighting, reached regulatory agreement for RRs and RDs

problems.evidence: Roughly 55% of the cohort has no recorded severity score at 12 months because registry visits are scheduled at 6-month intervals and only at clinician discretion. The measurement process is handled by five competing imputations rather than modeled as part of the causal structure, and the argument that the data are missing at random is that the imputed answers happened to match a trial result already known to the analysts.
problems.quote: The main limitation pertains to the amount of missing outcome data, with approximately 45% of the cohort having a recorded PASI at 12 months available for analysis

problems.evidence: No negative control, proxy or validation dataset enters the workflow. Unmeasured confounding is instead dismissed because the estimate matched CLEAR, which makes the replication itself the confounding diagnostic and leaves no procedure available when a reference trial does not exist. The same reasoning is then extended to the stable unit treatment value assumption.
problems.quote: This assumption is unlikely to be completely true, but given that the effect estimate in this study closely replicated that in the CLEAR trial, it is unlikely that any unmeasured confounding has important implications.

problems.evidence: One replication of one trial in one registry is converted into a warrant for reading other and future comparative effectiveness studies with confidence. Nothing in the study bounds how far that warrant travels: the agreement was demonstrated for a single drug pair, at a single time point, and only under the weighted estimator, since the matched estimator broke estimate agreement.
problems.quote: As a result, we believe that clinicians can interpret other or future comparative effectiveness studies with a target trial framework with confidence and use this information in shared decision-making as an adjunct to data from RCTs.

problems.evidence: The CLEAR result was known before the emulation was designed, and the risk is acknowledged without any procedure to neutralize it. The estimand, the 12-month severity threshold, was itself chosen because the registry supports it and the trial's own 16-week primary endpoint does not, so the target trial was fixed after seeing both the data and the answer it was being scored against.
problems.quote: An important bias to consider is that knowledge of the findings from the corresponding CLEAR trial may have altered the current study.

problems.evidence: The two treatment strategies are drug identities, not protocols. Dose and interval were left to each treating clinician, topical therapies were unrestricted and concomitant systemic therapies were permitted and adjusted for statistically, so the emulated arms pool treatment versions whose equivalence is assumed rather than defined, while CLEAR fixed dosing by protocol.
problems.quote: Dosing strategies were established by the individual clinicians.

papers.title: Emulating a Novel Clinical Trial Using Existing Observational Data. Predicting Results of the PreVent Study.
papers.one_line: Analysts blinded to the PreVent trial result registered an emulation using pooled data from three prior airway trials and predicted the direction of effect, with a mean difference in lowest oxygen saturation of 1.8% (95% CI -1.0 to 4.6) in 360 patients against 3.9% (95% CI 1.4 to 6.4) in the 401-patient trial.
papers.what_was_done: On 7 February 2019 the PreVent investigators handed deidentified patient-level data from three prior randomized airway management trials to an analysis team that did not know the trial result, and the team registered its analysis plan, code and results with an honest broker on 17 February 2019, before publication. The emulation used propensity score and coarsened exact matching to build 180 versus 180 groups from 360 patients, against 199 versus 202 in the trial. The primary outcome, lowest oxygen saturation, differed by 1.8 percentage points (CI -1.0 to 4.6) in the emulation and 3.9 (CI 1.4 to 6.4) in the trial, giving a difference-in-differences of -2.1% (CI -5.9 to 1.7). Severe hypoxemia below 80% occurred in 13.9% versus 23.3% in the emulation (risk ratio 0.60, CI 0.4 to 0.9) and 10.9% versus 22.8% in the trial (risk ratio 0.48, CI 0.3 to 0.8), giving a difference-in-differences of 2.5% (CI -8.1 to 13.6). The unadjusted observational comparison pointed the opposite way. Positive pressure delivered by noninvasive ventilation was pooled with bag-mask delivery in the emulation but not in the trial, and noninvasive ventilation in the 6 hours before intubation ran at 39.4% versus 22.1%. Exploratory outcomes could exclude little: ventilator-free days difference-in-differences -1.1 (CI -4.5 to 2.2), death before discharge 0.0% (CI -13.7 to 13.8).

future_research.gap: There is no accepted procedure for declaring an emulation to agree with the trial it emulated
future_research.quote:
Authoritative guidance for
comparing target trial emulations with
realized target trials does not yet exist

problems.evidence: Difference-in-differences estimates on the absolute scale are computed for every outcome, which is a calibrated comparison of estimands rather than a pass or fail label: -2.1% (CI -5.9 to 1.7) for lowest oxygen saturation and 2.5% (CI -8.1 to 13.6) for severe hypoxemia. What it does not close is the decision rule. The agreement criteria were not prespecified, no minimal clinically important difference was set, and the findings are consequently labelled exploratory.
problems.quote:
we
suggest using a prespeciﬁed minimal
clinically important difference in outcomes
and testing agreement with prespeciﬁed
statistical tests

problems.evidence: Blinding the analysts to the trial result and depositing the plan, the code and the results with an honest broker ten days before publication removes the specific route by which a target trial gets tuned to a known answer, and it is the only emulation reviewed here that does so. It does not remove the general problem: the analysts saw the observational data while choosing eligibility, matching scheme and exposure definition, and the agreement criteria were still chosen afterwards.
problems.quote:
The
analysts registered an analytical plan,
statistical code, and results of their
observational analysis

problems.evidence: The trial required positive pressure by bag-mask device; the emulation pooled bag-mask with noninvasive ventilation to avoid discarding a large group, so noninvasive ventilation in the prior 6 hours ran at 39.4% in the emulated treated arm against 22.1% in the trial arm. The paper concedes the two delivery routes may be a sufficiently different intervention, and no criterion decided that they belonged in one equivalence class.
problems.quote:
there could be differences in
positive-pressure ventilation delivered by
noninvasive ventilation versus bag-mask
device that render this a sufﬁciently different
intervention

problems.evidence: A single emulation of a single critical care trial, drawing on unusually rich trial-collected covariates including APACHE II score, induction oxygen saturation and reason for intubation, is concluded to support target trial emulation for comparative effectiveness research generally. The conditions that made it work, patient-level trial data rather than claims and a physiologic outcome measured within minutes, are named but not converted into any statement of where the conclusion stops.
problems.quote:
These ﬁndings support the
use of target trial emulation for comparative effectiveness research.

problems.evidence: Three completed randomized trials were pooled and the emulation still finished with 360 patients after matching, fewer than the 401 randomized in the trial being predicted. The emulated primary effect could not exclude zero at 1.8% (CI -1.0 to 4.6) while the trial's 3.9% (CI 1.4 to 6.4) could, and the reduced effective sample after matching is named as one reason.
problems.quote:
our smaller effective sample size after
matching

problems.evidence: Confounder control rested on a causal model built from content knowledge and published evidence, and residual confounding is left as an unquantified possibility. No negative control outcome, proxy or validation subsample is used, even though the design had an unusual asset for one: an unadjusted analysis that pointed the opposite way from both the adjusted analysis and the trial, which is a measured confounding signal never converted into a bound.
problems.quote:
although we used
both content knowledge and published
evidence to generate a causal model and
controlled for all relevant confounders
in that model

papers.title: Improving rheumatoid arthritis comparative effectiveness research through causal inference principles: systematic review using a target trial emulation framework.
papers.one_line: A systematic audit of 31 head-to-head comparative effectiveness studies of biologic DMARDs found that 29 (94%) carried at least one design limitation across seven target trial components, with 61% using post-baseline information in eligibility and 12 studies claiming per-protocol effects while none adjusted for time-varying confounding.
papers.what_was_done: Thirty-one head-to-head observational comparative effectiveness studies of biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs in rheumatoid arthritis were assessed against the seven components of a target trial protocol. Only one study explicitly emulated a target trial. Nineteen of 31 (61%) built eligibility on post-baseline information by requiring at least one follow-up visit or a minimum follow-up duration, with up to 69% of patients excluded on that basis, and seven more made the same exclusion implicitly through complete-case analysis, excluding up to 82%. Treatments were well defined but strategies were not: one study specified which treatment changes were protocol compliant. Thirteen (42%) used only prespecified confounders with no cited literature review or directed acyclic graph, five (16%) used only statistical variable selection, and nine (29%) adjusted for nothing. Six studies stated a causal contrast in advance; 20 implied an intention-to-treat effect of which 19 excluded patients without follow-up, and 12 implied per-protocol effects with none adjusting for post-baseline time-varying confounding. Seventeen used complete-case analysis, three used multiple imputation and nine used single imputation. Four studies performed sample size calculations, and arms as small as fewer than 50 patients drew no discussion of power.

future_research.gap: Adherence adjustment in this literature has not moved beyond methods that change the outcome definition
future_research.quote:
Future work in this area should
incorporate more modern approaches to adherence adjustment

problems.evidence: The dominant eligibility criterion in this literature is a healthcare-use event: having attended at least one follow-up visit. Nineteen of 31 studies impose it explicitly and seven more implicitly, excluding up to 69% and 82% of patients respectively. Attendance is influenced by both the drug started and the outcome, so the criterion conditions on a collider, and the review states the resulting bias can run in either direction.
problems.quote:
19 out of 31 (61%) studies explicitly included post-baseline information in their eligibility
criteria by requiring at least one follow-up

problems.evidence: Twelve studies declare or imply a per-protocol effect and none adjusts for the post-baseline time-varying confounding that per-protocol estimation requires, while ten artificially censor patients who discontinue the initial drug. The published quantity is a difference between adherers whose adherence is itself prognostic, reported under the label of the estimand the design cannot deliver.
problems.quote:
12 studies declared or implied per-protocol effects in part of
their analysis

problems.evidence: The drugs under comparison are unambiguous and the strategies are not. One study of 31 states which treatment changes count as protocol compliant, monotherapy studies leave unclear whether starting a conventional DMARD would be censored, and biosimilar switching and discontinuation for remission are not separated from failure. What counts as remaining on strategy had to be inferred from what each analysis censored.
problems.quote: Treatments under comparison were well defined, but not treatment strategies.

problems.evidence: Registry-scale data does not translate into analyzable sample. Arms fall below 50 patients after eligibility restriction and complete-case exclusion, four of 31 studies computed a sample size, and power limitations typically go undiscussed. The review states the underlying point directly: an underpowered observational study can at best emulate an underpowered trial, and sample size is not a design decision the investigator controls.
problems.quote:
There was typically
no discussion about power limitations, even when sample sizes were as small as <50 in
each arm

problems.evidence: Seventeen of 31 studies use complete-case analysis, nine use single imputation such as last observation carried forward or nonresponse imputation, and three use multiple imputation. Missingness is uniformly treated as a nuisance to remove, either by dropping the patient or by filling the value, and no study models attendance as part of the causal structure even though attendance is what the eligibility criteria condition on.
problems.quote: 17 out of 31 studies used complete-case analyses

problems.evidence: Twenty-nine of 31 published comparative effectiveness studies carry at least one bias-generating design limitation, and all 31 passed peer review as evidence about drug choice. No threshold exists that would have stopped any of them: not for how much post-baseline information may enter eligibility, not for how confounders may be selected when nine studies adjusted for none, and not for what sensitivity analysis is sufficient.
problems.quote: 94% had at least one design limitation with the potential to introduce bias

problems.evidence: The audit is component-wise, which is the first half of a decomposition: failures are attributed to eligibility (61%), causal contrast (81% undefined), assignment (42%), follow-up (six studies with no defined end) and analysis, rather than pooled into a single risk-of-bias verdict. It stops short of the second half. No component is assigned a magnitude, the direction of bias is left as either direction, and mapping loss is not separated from estimation error in any of the 31 studies.
problems.quote:
Study
designs were reviewed for seven components of the target trial emulation framework: eligibility
criteria, treatment strategies, assignment procedures, follow-up period, outcome, causal contrasts
of interest

papers.title: Target trial emulation: teaching epidemiology and beyond.
papers.one_line: A commentary arguing that trial emulation belongs in the introductory epidemiology curriculum and proposing that an emulation validated against a real trial can then be modified to answer questions the trial never asked, while conceding that the alignment between emulations and trials remains to be seen.
papers.what_was_done: The commentary accompanies a screening colonoscopy emulation and makes two arguments. The pedagogic one is that trial emulation needs no new vocabulary, notation or method beyond what is already taught about trials, so introductory courses require little augmentation and the framework makes the flaws in common analyses immediately visible; the worked example is that only the emulation reproduces the crossing cumulative incidence curves a screening trial would show. The methodological one is a program: an emulation whose short-term estimates match an ongoing trial's interim results may be trusted enough to act on before the trial matures, and an emulation validated against a completed trial may then be modified to estimate effects in a more heterogeneous population or on endpoints of interest rather than surrogate endpoints. The commentary lists the components that typically cannot be emulated: blinding, eligibility criteria forced by data availability, sufficient baseline confounders for exchangeability, and interventions that are not sufficiently well defined. It states that even successful emulation of random assignment does not guarantee comparability with real trials, and that the degree of alignment achieved so far remains to be seen.

future_research.gap: Whether emulations align with well-conducted trials is an open empirical question, and the studies that would answer it must be done before the trial reports
future_research.quote: The degree to which explicit target trial emulation in observational studies aligns with results from well-conducted trials remains to be seen.

future_research.gap: The creative extensions proposed have not been formalized or assessed
future_research.quote: (It will be important, of course, to formalize and assess any such broadened methods.)

problems.evidence: The extrapolation is proposed explicitly as a program: validate an emulation against a trial, then modify the target trial to change the population or swap a surrogate endpoint for a clinical one, and carry the validation forward. No condition is given under which agreement on the trial's own question licenses the modified question, and the commentary elsewhere concedes that population differences alone can make estimates differ.
problems.quote: we can modify the target trial in our observational analysis to estimate other quantities such as effects in a more heterogeneous population or effects on endpoints of interest rather than surrogate endpoints

problems.evidence: An ill-defined intervention is treated as something the framework makes visible rather than something it resolves. Making the analyst see the tradeoff does not tell them what estimand the data-defined intervention actually delivers, and the commentary's own remedy list stops at proceeding while conscious of the compromise or abandoning the question.
problems.quote: our intervention of interest may not be sufficiently well-defined, and describing the ill-defined target trial forces us to see that tradeoff

problems.evidence: The decision rule offered is whether the tradeoffs are too big, with nothing that measures them. Blinding that cannot be emulated, eligibility criteria forced by data availability, insufficient confounders and ill-defined interventions are listed as compromises of the same kind, and no accounting separates the loss from each, or separates any of them from estimation error.
problems.quote: In other cases, we may realize the trial we are able to emulate is making tradeoffs that are too big and we may therefore choose to refine our questions or seek other data.

problems.evidence: Eligibility criteria chosen because of what the data record are named as a routine and accepted compromise. Nothing distinguishes a criterion the data can verify from one the data cannot express, and the commentary offers no way to tell which population the resulting emulation actually enrolled.
problems.quote: we may be forced to choose different eligibility criteria due to data availability considerations

problems.evidence: Adoption of the framework is recommended independently of whether emulations turn out to agree with trials, on the grounds that the principles encourage known good practices. That severs the design label from any evidence about the assumption burden a labelled study carries, in the same paragraph that concedes the alignment question is unresolved.
problems.quote: We believe, however, that the principles behind trial emulation ought to be adopted regardless because they encourage known good practices.

problems.evidence: When an emulation disagrees with the trial it emulates, the proposed response is to re-examine what unmeasured confounding could remain, a diagnostic that exists only when a trial is available to disagree with. No negative control, proxy or validation dataset is offered for the ordinary case in which no trial exists, which is the case the commentary elsewhere says emulation is especially for.
problems.quote: it may motivated us to re-examine the means by which we emulated random assignment (e.g., what unmeasured confounding could remain?)
